title: Jeep Cherokee Engines by Year (1974–2023)
description: Every factory engine in the Jeep Cherokee by year: AMC sixes and V8s in the full-size SJ, the XJ's 2.5 and 4.0, and the 2014–2023 2.4, 3.2 and 2.0 turbo.
intro: Jeep has used the Cherokee name on three different vehicles in the US: a two-door version of the full-size Wagoneer (1974–1983), the compact unibody XJ (1984–2001), and a front-drive-based model sold from 2014 to 2023. The 2002–2012 US model in between was sold as the Liberty.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: SJ (full-size)
intro: The full-size Cherokee used AMC's 258 six and 360 and 401 V8s. Jeep's literature stopped quoting horsepower after 1974, so most later years show no rating.

generations.name: XJ
intro: The XJ started with AMC's 2.5 four, a GM-built 2.8 V6 and a Renault 2.1 turbodiesel. The 4.0 six replaced the V6 for 1987 and was rated 190 hp from 1991.

generations.name: KL
intro: The last Cherokee offered the 2.4 Tigershark four, the 3.2 Pentastar V6 and, from 2019, a 2.0 turbo four.

excluded.researchNote: Off Road Xtreme says both 360s continued for 1979; the 1979 factory brochure and the FSJ table list only the 2-bbl. Factory evidence says not offered; do not publish without another source.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
